artworks.medium: Space
artworks.description: Renovated for the museum’s 2025 reopening: buy tickets here (or show your online ticket, good any day), leave backpacks, large bags, racquets and drinks, and take the stairs or elevator up to the museum on the second floor. Audio tours in English, Spanish, French, German and Italian.

artworks.title: Newport Tennis Traditions Gallery
artworks.medium: Gallery
artworks.placeNote: The museum publishes no gallery plan: the place is approximate.
artworks.description: Celebrates the origins of tennis in Newport and its link with the US Open, which began on the Casino’s lawns in 1881 as the U.S. National Championships, with the perpetual US Open trophies on display.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the International Tennis Hall of Fame’s own pages

artworks.title: The Birth of Tennis (1874–1918)
artworks.medium: Gallery
artworks.placeNote: The museum publishes no gallery plan: the place is approximate.

artworks.descriptionKind: From the International Tennis Hall of Fame’s own pages

artworks.title: The Popular Game (1918–1968)
artworks.medium: Gallery
artworks.placeNote: The museum publishes no gallery plan: the place is approximate.
artworks.description: Tennis between the wars and after: the stars of the amateur era, the pros who toured for money, and the fashion, racquets and trophies of fifty years.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the International Tennis Hall of Fame’s own pages

artworks.title: The Open Era (1968–today)
artworks.medium: Gallery
artworks.placeNote: The museum publishes no gallery plan: the place is approximate.
artworks.description: From 1968, when amateurs and professionals could at last play the same tournaments, to today’s champions: match-worn clothes, racquets and trophies.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the International Tennis Hall of Fame’s own pages

artworks.title: René Lacoste’s “Crocodile” blazer
artworks.medium: Clothing
artworks.placeNote: The museum publishes no gallery plan: the place is approximate.
artworks.description: From the museum’s fashion archive: the blazer of the French champion René Lacoste, nicknamed “the Crocodile”, with the crocodile emblem that later became his shirt brand. artworks.title: The Art of Tennis
artworks.medium: Art
artworks.placeNote: The museum publishes no gallery plan: the place is approximate.

artworks.title: Ashe ’68 VR experience
artworks.medium: Interactive
artworks.placeNote: The museum publishes no gallery plan: the place is approximate.

artworks.descriptionKind: From the International Tennis Hall of Fame’s own pages

artworks.placeNote: The museum publishes no gallery plan: the place is approximate.

artworks.title: The Newport Casino on Bellevue Avenue
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.galleryName: The entrance arch from Bellevue Avenue, through the Casino building to the Lawn
artworks.description: McKim, Mead & White’s first major commission, built in 1880 for James Gordon Bennett Jr., publisher of the New York Herald: shops and a restaurant on the street, club rooms above, in shingle, stone and brick. One of the finest Shingle Style buildings in America, a National Historic Landmark since 1987. Photo 1970.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record
artworks.imageCredit: Historic American Buildings Survey (Library of Congress, HABS RI-331), public domain

artworks.title: The Casino’s Bellevue Avenue elevation
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.galleryName: The entrance arch from Bellevue Avenue, through the Casino building to the Lawn
artworks.description: The architects’ drawing of the street front. Despite its name, the Casino never had gambling: “casino” comes from the Italian casina, a small social building on a country estate.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record

artworks.title: The Lawn and the clock tower
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.description: The grass court inside the Casino, framed by the Horseshoe Piazza and its clock tower. On August 31, 1881 the first U.S. National Men’s Singles Championship, today’s US Open, was played at the Casino, with a string quartet; it stayed here until 1914.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record

artworks.title: The interior court, looking south (1970)
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.description: The Historic American Buildings Survey’s photograph of the court and the clock tower from the entrance.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record
artworks.imageCredit: Historic American Buildings Survey (Library of Congress, HABS RI-331), public domain

artworks.title: Tennis at the Casino, 1880s
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.galleryName: The Horseshoe Piazza with its clock tower, the 1881 Club (members’ and event space) wrapped round the Lawn
artworks.description: Watching tennis through the Casino’s lattice. Archery, billiards, concerts, dancing, horse shows, lawn bowling and theatricals filled its summers; on opening day in 1880 more than 3,000 people came to look.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record

artworks.title: Bill Talbert Center Court
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.galleryName: Bill Talbert Center Court, the stadium court of the Hall of Fame Open
artworks.description: The stadium court of the Hall of Fame Open (ATP Challenger and WTA 125, every July), named for the Hall of Famer Bill Talbert. The grass courts were completely renovated in 2020; the public can book them in season (May to October) at the Pro Shop, 401-849-4777.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record

artworks.title: The Casino Theatre
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.description: Stanford White’s theatre and ballroom for 300, with removable seats; its gold-trimmed ivory interior had a sky-blue ceiling with golden stars. Photo 1970.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record
artworks.imageCredit: Historic American Buildings Survey (Library of Congress, HABS RI-331), public domain

artworks.title: The Casino Theatre in its heyday
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.description: An old photograph of the theatre’s entrance from the museum’s archive.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record

artworks.title: James Gordon Bennett Jr.
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.description: The Casino’s founder. Legend says he built it after his polo partner, Captain Henry Candy, rode a horse onto the porch of the gentlemen’s Newport Reading Room on a bet and lost his guest membership; in fact Bennett had planned a social club since 1878.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record

artworks.title: Jimmy Van Alen, founder of the Hall of Fame
artworks.medium: Historic grounds
artworks.description: When the Casino was in danger of demolition in the 1950s, its president Jimmy Van Alen and his wife Candy founded a National Tennis Hall of Fame here, after visiting baseball’s Hall of Fame. Van Alen also invented the tiebreak. The International Tennis Federation recognized the Hall in 1986.
artworks.descriptionKind: From the Hall of Fame’s Historic Grounds page and the HABS record
